classes.label: Code edit
classes.description: Write, change, refactor or extend code or files in a software project.

rules: Read a file before you change it, and run the project's check or tests after each change.

classes.label: Debug
classes.description: Find and fix a bug, a failing test, an error message or a crash.

rules: Reproduce the failure first, change one thing at a time, and quote the result line of the check.

classes.label: UI design
classes.description: The look of a web page or an app: layout, visual style, colours, typography, UI and UX.

classes.label: Drawing
classes.description: Draw, paint or animate a picture or a portrait with code: a sketch, line art, SVG or canvas art.

classes.label: 3D scene
classes.description: A 3D scene or model: Three.js, WebGL, voxels, a photo rebuilt in 3D.

classes.label: Writing
classes.description: Write prose in words, not code: an essay, an article, a story, an email, a letter, a post or documentation text.

classes.label: Plan
classes.description: Plan an approach, a design or an architecture before building it, or break the work into steps.

classes.label: Research
classes.description: Look something up, compare options, or explain how something works.

classes.label: Summarize
classes.description: Summarize, shorten or pull the key points out of text that is given, or compress a conversation.

classes.label: Chat
classes.description: Small talk, a greeting, thanks, a short question with a short answer, or an instruction about the reply itself (answer in one word, say OK, confirm, stop) that asks for no work: no code, files, commands or git.

classifier.question: What kind of work does this request ask for?
classifier.package_question: Which of these instructions fits this request best?

reading.text: Build it as {reading}. The request could also mean {other}, so start your answer with one short line that says how you read it, for example: "Building it as {reading}. Say if you wanted {other}." Then go straight on; do not stop to ask first.

low.note: Reasoning effort is set to low. Keep your thinking brief and focused, moving directly to the conclusion without unnecessary elaboration.

high.note: Reasoning effort for this step is high. Think the task through and check your plan against the code before you act.

xhigh.note: Reasoning effort is set to xhigh. Please think carefully through the task, validate key assumptions, consider plausible alternatives, and prioritize correctness, consistency, and clarity in the final answer.
